transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-11-13
Time: 15:00 PST
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Jordan (Redwood AE), Maya (Redwood SE), Arjun (Redwood Partner Eng), Lena (CTO - ArborBank), Marcus (Head of Platform), Priya (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be noisy):
- Walkthrough of vendor listing preflight requirements, VPC/KMS onramp, and quantization lab plan.
- Customer to provide CIDRs, KMS vendor/domain, and sample traffic patterns.
- Redwood to provision Dedicated staging instance and run quant lab with 8-bit/4-bit settings; follow up with perf matrix.

Topics covered:
- Marketplace vendor listing checklist and governance artifacts
- VPC peering vs TGW options for private deployments
- KMS/HSM compatibility and key rotation expectations
- Quantization tradeoffs (int8 vs int4) and sample quality/regression tests
- Telemetry, audit logs, and RBAC mapping for joint solution

Transcript (timestamps approximate, transcription imperfect):
[00:00] Jordan: hey everyone, thanks for joining. i think we have an hour, hour plus, uh, for this vendor listing and the quant lab plan. quick intros?
[00:18] Lena: lena here, CTO at arbor bank. Marcus is with me, and priya will cover security bits. thanks for coordinating.
[00:28] Jordan: perfect. maya and arjun from our side?
[00:31] Maya: yeah maya lopez, solutions engineering. hi all.
[00:33] Arjun: arjun mehta, partner engineering, i'll be the liaison for marketplace packaging and the listing artifacts.
[00:38] Marcus: great, thanks. high level context — we're evaluating vendors for a regulated deployment, need private network, audit, and predictable latency under 120ms p95 for our customer-facing chat flows.
[00:52] Jordan: ok, that's helpful. are you leaning hosted vs dedicated or will this be private everywhere?
[00:58] Marcus: primary is private — we need VPC connectivity to our accounts and KMS control. Hosted only for non-prod maybe.
[01:05] Priya: compliance — SOC2 in scope, also internal audit wants key ownership in our KMS. any vendor-managed keys are a no-go.
[01:13] Maya: totally understood. so for Redwood Private we can run in your VPC with customer-managed keys; we support KMS integrations — we also do HSM through our partner vendor, though i think the name in the doc was mis-typed as "H-S-Mi" sometimes.
[01:27] Marcus: uh yeah we saw a note about an HSM add-on, what's the operational impact?
[01:31] Arjun: overhead is mostly network and key policy — you bring the key, we configure the service principal to use EKM. We'll share our KMS mapping doc.
[01:40] Lena: and for the listing we need the reference architecture diagram and minimal helm chart for our engineers to vet.
[01:47] Jordan: yep — we have a vendor listing pack: diagram, manifests, security checklist, audit log sample, and runbook. we'll attach the checklist after.
[01:54] Marcus: cool. on network, are you recommending VPC peering or Transit Gateway? peering has tedious route tables for us.
[02:03] Maya: we generally recommend TGW for multi-account private deploys; peering ok for single-account, but TGW reduces route churn. small caveat is TGW cross-region costs — you might see bandwidth charges.
[02:14] Priya: is there a requirement for NAT egress? we need egress to telemetry endpoints but must restrict outbound to allowlist.
[02:21] Arjun: yep we support egress controls — you can lock down to our telemetry collector endpoints; we provide IP ranges and ASN list but note that the ranges could change during scaling. we'll version them and publish a CIDR list.
[02:35] Marcus: send the CIDR list. we'll need to plug into our firewall change window.
[02:40] Jordan: noted — action for redwood to share ranges.
[02:45] Maya: moving to the quantization lab — we propose a two-week lab: week one int8 sweeps, week two int4 experiments with per-prompt evals. objective: find lowest-bit variant with <2% degradation on our NPS prompt set.
[02:58] Lena: sounds reasonable. sample size? we have about 5k user-facing prompts in auth flows and 12k async queries in batch.
[03:07] Maya: for latency, what's your p95 SLA target again?
[03:09] Marcus: 120ms p95 for interactive flows.
[03:13] Maya: ok. note that int4 sometimes increases context compaction but can add decode variance; we'll measure token latency at 512 tokens and at your typical 120 token average.
[03:26] Priya: also need to understand audit surface — when you say audit logs, do logs live in our S3 or do they stream to your observability?
[03:33] Arjun: option A: logs go to your S3 via our connector; option B: we retain short-term logs in our console (redwood con-sul?) and you pull via API. For regulatory reasons you can opt for S3 export only.
[03:47] Priya: S3 export only preferred. we need retention controls and KMS encryption on the bucket.
[03:53] Jordan: we can support that. we'll include the S3 export doc and sample bucket policy.
[03:58] [05:02] Speaker 1 (automated note): recording paused, resumed.
[05:10] Maya: quick note about marketplace listing gating: some customers need an independent security attestation; we can include a penetration test summary and SOC-2 artifact in the listing package.
[05:22] Lena: perfect — that will speed legal review.
[05:26] Marcus: on the pilot, we want to run a traffic replay into a dedicated staging instance that mirrors prod data rates (masked). can redwood host that?
[05:36] Arjun: yes — we can provision a Redwood Dedicated staging pod in your account or in our dedicated pool with isolated tenancy. provisioning lead time ~48–72 hours once CIDRs and KMS details are provided.
[05:50] Marcus: prefer in our account so traffic doesn't egress externally.
[05:54] Jordan: good call — private deployment in your account is supported; we'll need an IAM role spec and list of required ports.
[06:02] Priya: who manages AMIs/containers? we need provenance and scanning proof.
[06:07] Maya: image provenance: we provide signed images and attestations; third-party scan report can be included in the listing docs. we'll add that as well.
[06:16] Lena: can you walk us through quantization tradeoffs briefly? i know the term but want practical expectations.
[06:22] Maya: sure — so int8 quant usually reduces model size by ~2x with negligible quality reduction for conversational prompts; int4 can reduce size further but risk higher perplexity in niche prompts. we run eval suites: ROUGE/BLEU less useful for chat; better to use human evals or your internal quality metric, e.g., our suggested 'intent-stability' script.
[06:42] Marcus: what's the difference in throughput and memory footprint?
[06:46] Maya: int8 gives about 1.8x throughput improvement on A100-like hardware; int4 maybe 2.5x but depends on kernel support. if you plan to use onboard inference accelerators we should verify kernel availability.
[06:58] Arjun: note that some older GPUs may not have optimized int4 kernels and fallback takes CPU kernel path which hurts latency. we'll include a hardware compatibility matrix in the lab doc.
[07:12] Priya: for our auditors, we need deterministic key rotation logs if you're using customer KMS. can you show rotation proof?
[07:19] Jordan: yes — rotation events are logged with request IDs and we can provide a sample export.
[07:24] Lena: ok, now listing packaging: what's the minimal deliverable for marketplace acceptance?
[07:30] Arjun: minimal: 1) Reference architecture diagram; 2) Helm chart or manifest with variables; 3) Security checklist and SOC-2 attestation; 4) Quickstart demo with sample traffic and smoke tests; 5) Pricing/commit options doc.
[07:44] Marcus: for manifests, do you support helm v3 and kustomize?
[07:48] Maya: helm v3 yes, kustomize we can include overlays. we also provide a terraform module if you prefer infra as code.
[07:56] Lena: is there a marketplace billing integration? we need consolidated billing via marketplace or direct contract?
[08:02] Jordan: we support both. Marketplace listing can enable consolidated billing; for enterprise SLA and dedicated capacity often customers choose direct contract for reserved capacity.
[08:13] Marcus: pricing transparency is huge — we need token-level cost breakdowns during the pilot.
[08:18] Maya: we'll instrument token-level telemetry in the lab and share token-by-route cost.
[08:24] [08:45] Maya: quick follow: sample prompts — can you share a small subset now?
[08:50] Lena: i'll upload a masked set after the call, about 500 prompts representative across flows.
[08:55] Marcus: and a note on privacy — those prompts should be handled under our NDA and scrubbed.
[08:59] Jordan: confirmed. we'll use your scrubbed set.
[09:04] Priya: one more on RBAC — how granular is role mapping? we have devs, ops, auditors; auditors need read-only access to logs and compliance artifacts.
[09:13] Arjun: RBAC maps to your SAML groups; we support roles: admin, operator, viewer, auditor. we'll include a mapping guide for SAML attributes and group sync.
[09:24] Lena: ok. timeline recap? we'd like pilot started by next week.
[09:29] Jordan: action recap: Marcus to send CIDRs/KMS details by Tue (11/16); Maya will produce quant lab runbook and provisioning checklist by Thu (11/18); Jordan will send pricing/commit options by Wed (11/17). Arjun will attach listing artifacts template.
[09:47] Marcus: that's fine, we'll try to hit Tue for the CIDRs.
[09:52] Lena: legal will need the SOC-2 and pen test summary, please attach to the listing packet.
[09:58] Jordan: will do.
[10:02] [10:30] Speaker 2: (background) noise, small cross talk.
[10:36] Marcus: one technical wrinkle — we use a private NAT gateway pattern; our security team prefers no internet egress from prod nodes. can the telemetry collector pull via VPC endpoint?
[10:45] Arjun: yes we can support VPC endpoint ingestion for telemetry; we need to publish the schema and provide client config.
[10:53] Priya: will telemetry include PII? we need field-level redaction at source.
[10:58] Maya: we'll apply PII filters in the ingestion pipeline; still recommend you scrub before replay.
[11:06] Lena: any blockers you see for a fast pilot?
[11:09] Maya: blockers: CIDR/KMS details, masked prompt set, and a 2-hour window for our infra team to run provisioning. nothing major.
[11:18] Jordan: ok, timeline again — provisioning lead time 48–72 hours once we have details; quant lab results within two weeks of staging availability.
[11:27] Marcus: sounds good.
[11:32] Priya: for the listing packet, can you include a minimal compliance matrix mapping Redwood controls to our control IDs?
[11:40] Arjun: yes. we'll produce a controls mapping spreadsheet.
[11:45] Jordan: any competitor concerns? lena — you mentioned earlier some vendors that promised lower costs.
[11:50] Lena: yes, a couple vendors said lower cost but they had limited audit coverage. this is why we need the attestations.
[11:58] Maya: understood. we'll provide the attestation artifacts and the pilot perf numbers so you can compare apples-to-apples.
[12:05] Jordan: ok unless anything else, we'll wrap. thanks everyone.
[12:09] Lena: thanks, great session.
[12:11] Marcus: thanks.
[12:14] Priya: thanks all.

Meeting recap (auto):
- Customer asks for private deployment with customer-managed KMS, TGW recommended for multi-account, S3-only audit export preferred.
- Redwood to provision Dedicated staging in-customer-account and run quantization experiments (int8/int4) against masked prompt set.
- Listing package to include SOC-2, pentest summary, reference architecture, helm manifests, and controls mapping.
- Next steps and action items captured.

References and attachments mentioned (to be shared via email/drive):
- Vendor listing checklist (Redwood)
- KMS integration mapping document
- Helm chart sample and terraform module
- Quantization lab runbook and perf spreadsheet template
